title: Reading the Air Trapped in Ice
body:
The atmosphere leaves no fossils, yet climate scientists can state with confidence what the air contained eight hundred thousand years ago. The evidence comes from Antarctica, where snow that fell in a single season has never melted and has instead been buried by the snow of the seasons that followed. As the accumulated weight compresses the layers beneath, the loose crystals at the surface are gradually welded into solid ice, and the spaces between them shrink until they close entirely. Whatever air occupied those spaces at the moment of closure is sealed off, and remains sealed for as long as the ice endures.

A core drilled from such a sheet is therefore a sequence of samples rather than a single specimen. Bubbles near the top hold air from the industrial era; those a kilometer down hold air from the last glacial maximum. Extracting the gas is mechanically simple, since crushing a fragment of ice in a vacuum releases it, and the resulting sample can be measured by the same instruments used on air collected yesterday. The concentrations of carbon dioxide and methane that emerge are not inferred from proxies. They are direct measurements of ancient atmosphere. This distinguishes them from most of what is known about the deep past, which reaches us only through substitutes: the width of a tree ring standing for a summer, the chemistry of a shell standing for the temperature of the water that formed it.

Dating the layers demands more ingenuity. Near the surface, annual accumulation is visible, and the layers can be counted much as one counts the rings of a tree. Deeper down the layers thin under pressure until counting becomes impossible, and researchers must instead model how the ice has flowed, calibrating their calculations against markers of known age. Volcanic eruptions are especially useful, because each deposits a distinctive film of sulfate that appears simultaneously in cores from opposite ends of the earth and thus anchors separate records to a common chronology. A large eruption is in this sense a stopwatch pressed once and read in both hemispheres.

One complication deserves emphasis. Because bubbles do not close until the snow above has buried them under roughly a hundred meters of accumulation, the air in any layer is invariably younger than the ice enclosing it. The offset can exceed several thousand years where accumulation is slow, and it must be estimated and subtracted before gas and temperature can be compared. Failing to account for it would distort the very relationship the cores are drilled to investigate, since an apparent lag between warming and rising carbon dioxide might be an artifact of the sealing process rather than a fact about the climate. Much of the technical literature on ice cores concerns not the measurements themselves, which are comparatively straightforward, but the corrections that make them mean anything.

questions.question: According to paragraph 1, how does ancient air become trapped in an ice sheet?

choices.A: Meltwater refreezes around pockets of air near the surface
choices.B: Gas rises from the bedrock and is captured by the overlying ice
choices.C: The spaces between snow crystals shrink and eventually close as the layers are compressed
choices.D: Wind drives air into cracks that later fill with snow

questions.explanation: 第1段落に "the spaces between them shrink until they close entirely. Whatever air occupied those spaces at the moment of closure is sealed off" とあり、圧縮によって隙間が閉じることで空気が封じ込められる。Aは本文が "has never melted" と述べる点と矛盾し、BとDは本文に記述がない。

questions.question: Why does the author state that the measurements "are not inferred from proxies"?

choices.A: To emphasize that ice cores yield the ancient atmosphere itself rather than an indirect indicator of it
choices.B: To argue that other methods of studying past climate have been abandoned
choices.C: To explain why the instruments must be calibrated before each use
choices.D: To indicate that the gas concentrations are still a matter of dispute

questions.explanation: 直後の "They are direct measurements of ancient atmosphere" が言い換えとして続いており、間接指標との対比によって証拠の直接性を強調するのが目的である。Bのように他手法の放棄は述べられておらず、Dは "direct measurements" という断定と矛盾する。

questions.question: The word "anchors" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to
questions.explanation: 火山灰の層が "appears simultaneously in cores from opposite ends of the earth" ことで、離れた記録を共通の年代尺度に固定する働きを述べている。したがって D の fixes が最も近い。A の compares は記録同士を比べるだけで、基準に固定するという意味を持たない。

questions.question: It can be inferred from paragraph 4 that a researcher who ignored the age offset might

choices.A: underestimate the total depth of the ice sheet
choices.B: conclude wrongly that temperature rose before carbon dioxide did
choices.C: fail to detect the sulfate layers left by volcanic eruptions
choices.D: overstate the amount of methane present during glacial periods

questions.explanation: 本文は "an apparent lag between warming and rising carbon dioxide might be an artifact of the sealing process" と述べている。空気が氷より新しい分を補正しなければ、二酸化炭素の上昇が実際より遅く見え、温暖化が先行したという誤った結論に至りうる。A、C、Dは補正の対象と無関係である。

questions.question: The word "them" in paragraph 4 ("the corrections that make them mean anything") refers to
questions.explanation: 当該文は "concerns not the measurements themselves, which are comparatively straightforward, but the corrections that make them mean anything" という構造で、補正が意味を与える対象は測定値である。Aは補正自身を指すことになり文意が循環し、Dは補正が扱う対象ではない。

atmosphere.etymology: ギリシャ語 atmos(蒸気) + sphaira(球) → 「蒸気の球」
atmosphere.usage_in_passage: 冒頭 "The atmosphere leaves no fossils" が本文の問題設定。化石を残さないはずの対象をどう知るのか、という問いが全体を貫く。
atmosphere.context_sentence: The atmosphere leaves no fossils, yet climate scientists can state with confidence what the air contained eight hundred thousand years ago.

fossils.etymology: ラテン語 fodere(掘る) → fossilis「掘り出されたもの」+ -s
fossils.usage_in_passage: 通常の古生物学的証拠を指し、それが存在しないという事実が氷床コアの価値を際立たせる。
fossils.context_sentence: The atmosphere leaves no fossils, yet climate scientists can state with confidence what the air contained eight hundred thousand years ago.

climate.etymology: ギリシャ語 klima(傾き、地帯) → ラテン語 clima
climate.usage_in_passage: "climate scientists" として研究主体を、末尾では "a fact about the climate" として研究対象を指す。
climate.context_sentence: The atmosphere leaves no fossils, yet climate scientists can state with confidence what the air contained eight hundred thousand years ago.

scientists.etymology: ラテン語 scire(知る) → science + -ist + -s
scientists.usage_in_passage: "can state with confidence" の主語となり、主張の確からしさを担保する存在として提示される。
scientists.context_sentence: The atmosphere leaves no fossils, yet climate scientists can state with confidence what the air contained eight hundred thousand years ago.

confidence.etymology: ラテン語 con-(強意) + fidere(信じる) → confidere + -ence
confidence.usage_in_passage: "state with confidence" が、化石が無いにもかかわらず断定できるという逆説を作り、その根拠を示す義務を本文に課す。
confidence.context_sentence: The atmosphere leaves no fossils, yet climate scientists can state with confidence what the air contained eight hundred thousand years ago.

hundred.etymology: 古英語 hundred。ゲルマン系の数詞
hundred.usage_in_passage: "eight hundred thousand years ago" で復元可能な時間の長さを、第4段落では "a hundred meters" で気泡が閉じる深さを示す。
hundred.context_sentence: The atmosphere leaves no fossils, yet climate scientists can state with confidence what the air contained eight hundred thousand years ago.

thousand.etymology: 古英語 þūsend。ゲルマン系の数詞
thousand.usage_in_passage: 八十万年という桁を示し、氷床コアが扱う時間規模を読者に印象づける。
thousand.context_sentence: The atmosphere leaves no fossils, yet climate scientists can state with confidence what the air contained eight hundred thousand years ago.

fell.etymology: 古英語 feallan(落ちる)の過去形。ゲルマン系
fell.usage_in_passage: "snow that fell in a single season" が、後の層序の議論の出発点となる一回の降雪を指す。
fell.context_sentence: The evidence comes from Antarctica, where snow that fell in a single season has never melted and has instead been buried by the snow of the seasons that followed.

melted.etymology: 古英語 meltan(溶ける)。ゲルマン系
melted.usage_in_passage: "has never melted" が南極の記録が連続している理由であり、Q1の誤答選択肢を排除する根拠にもなる。
melted.context_sentence: The evidence comes from Antarctica, where snow that fell in a single season has never melted and has instead been buried by the snow of the seasons that followed.

buried.etymology: 古英語 byrgan(埋める) → bury + -ed。ゲルマン系
buried.usage_in_passage: 第1段落では雪が後続の雪に埋もれる過程を、第4段落では気泡が百メートル下に埋もれるまで閉じない事実を述べ、同じ語が記録の生成と誤差の原因の両方を担う。
buried.context_sentence: The evidence comes from Antarctica, where snow that fell in a single season has never melted and has instead been buried by the snow of the seasons that followed.

accumulated.etymology: ラテン語 ad-(に) + cumulus(積み重ね) → accumulare + -ed
accumulated.usage_in_passage: "the accumulated weight compresses the layers beneath" が圧密の原動力を示す。
accumulated.context_sentence: As the accumulated weight compresses the layers beneath, the loose crystals at the surface are gradually welded into solid ice, and the spaces between them shrink until they close entirely.

compresses.etymology: ラテン語 com-(共に) + premere(押す) → 「押し縮める」
compresses.usage_in_passage: 積雪の重みが下層に働く力を示し、結晶が氷へ変わる過程を導入する。
compresses.context_sentence: As the accumulated weight compresses the layers beneath, the loose crystals at the surface are gradually welded into solid ice, and the spaces between them shrink until they close entirely.

beneath.etymology: 古英語 beneoðan(下に)。ゲルマン系
beneath.usage_in_passage: 圧縮される対象が下層であることを示し、深さと時代が対応する構造を暗示する。
beneath.context_sentence: As the accumulated weight compresses the layers beneath, the loose crystals at the surface are gradually welded into solid ice, and the spaces between them shrink until they close entirely.

loose.etymology: 古ノルド語 lauss(緩い)。ゲルマン系
loose.usage_in_passage: "the loose crystals at the surface" が変化の前の状態を示し、solid ice との対比を作る。
loose.context_sentence: As the accumulated weight compresses the layers beneath, the loose crystals at the surface are gradually welded into solid ice, and the spaces between them shrink until they close entirely.

gradually.etymology: ラテン語 gradus(段階) → gradual + -ly
gradually.usage_in_passage: 雪から氷への転換が瞬間的ではないことを示し、気泡が閉じるまでに時間差が生じる第4段落の伏線となる。
gradually.context_sentence: As the accumulated weight compresses the layers beneath, the loose crystals at the surface are gradually welded into solid ice, and the spaces between them shrink until they close entirely.

welded.etymology: 中世スウェーデン語 välla(沸かして接合する)由来。ゲルマン系
welded.usage_in_passage: "welded into solid ice" が、粒どうしが圧力で一体化する現象を金属加工の比喩で表す。
welded.context_sentence: As the accumulated weight compresses the layers beneath, the loose crystals at the surface are gradually welded into solid ice, and the spaces between them shrink until they close entirely.

shrink.etymology: 古英語 scrincan(縮む)。ゲルマン系
shrink.usage_in_passage: "the spaces between them shrink until they close entirely" が空気封入の直接の仕組みで、Q1の正解根拠となる。
shrink.context_sentence: As the accumulated weight compresses the layers beneath, the loose crystals at the surface are gradually welded into solid ice, and the spaces between them shrink until they close entirely.

entirely.etymology: ラテン語 integer(手つかずの) → entire + -ly
entirely.usage_in_passage: 隙間が部分的にではなく完全に閉じることを示し、封入の不可逆性を強調する。
entirely.context_sentence: As the accumulated weight compresses the layers beneath, the loose crystals at the surface are gradually welded into solid ice, and the spaces between them shrink until they close entirely.

occupied.etymology: ラテン語 ob-(に) + capere(取る) → occupare + -ed
occupied.usage_in_passage: "Whatever air occupied those spaces at the moment of closure" が、保存されるのが封入時点の空気であるという限定を与える。
occupied.context_sentence: Whatever air occupied those spaces at the moment of closure is sealed off, and remains sealed for as long as the ice endures.

closure.etymology: ラテン語 claudere(閉じる) → clausura + -ure
closure.usage_in_passage: "at the moment of closure" が時刻を定める語で、第4段落の年代のずれはこの瞬間と氷の形成時点の差から生じる。
closure.context_sentence: Whatever air occupied those spaces at the moment of closure is sealed off, and remains sealed for as long as the ice endures.

sealed.etymology: ラテン語 signum(印) → sigillum → seal + -ed
sealed.usage_in_passage: 同一文で二度用いられ、封入が起きることと持続することの両方を述べる。
sealed.context_sentence: Whatever air occupied those spaces at the moment of closure is sealed off, and remains sealed for as long as the ice endures.

endures.etymology: ラテン語 in-(中に) + durus(硬い) → indurare → endure + -s
endures.definition: 存続する、持ちこたえる。
endures.usage_in_passage: "for as long as the ice endures" が保存期間の条件を示し、氷が失われれば記録も失われることを含意する。
endures.context_sentence: Whatever air occupied those spaces at the moment of closure is sealed off, and remains sealed for as long as the ice endures.

drilled.etymology: 中低ドイツ語 drillen(穴を開ける)。ゲルマン系
drilled.usage_in_passage: 第2段落では試料採取の手段として、第4段落では "the cores are drilled to investigate" として研究目的を示す文脈で用いられる。
drilled.context_sentence: A core drilled from such a sheet is therefore a sequence of samples rather than a single specimen.

specimen.etymology: ラテン語 specere(見る) → specimen「見本」
specimen.usage_in_passage: "a sequence of samples rather than a single specimen" が、コアの本質が単一の物体ではなく時系列であることを示す。
specimen.context_sentence: A core drilled from such a sheet is therefore a sequence of samples rather than a single specimen.

bubbles.etymology: 中英語 bobel(泡)。擬音語的なゲルマン系の語 + -s
bubbles.usage_in_passage: 本文の中心的な対象。第2段落では深さごとの年代差を、第4段落では閉鎖の遅れによる誤差を担う。
bubbles.context_sentence: Bubbles near the top hold air from the industrial era; those a kilometer down hold air from the last glacial maximum.

kilometer.etymology: ギリシャ語 khilioi(千) + metron(尺度)
kilometer.usage_in_passage: "those a kilometer down" が深さと年代の対応を具体的な数字で示す。
kilometer.context_sentence: Bubbles near the top hold air from the industrial era; those a kilometer down hold air from the last glacial maximum.

glacial.usage_in_passage: "the last glacial maximum" が、深部の気泡が対応する時代を特定し、コアの射程を示す。
glacial.context_sentence: Bubbles near the top hold air from the industrial era; those a kilometer down hold air from the last glacial maximum.

extracting.etymology: ラテン語 ex-(外に) + trahere(引く) → extract + -ing
extracting.usage_in_passage: "Extracting the gas is mechanically simple" が、測定の技術的容易さを述べ、第4段落の「難しいのは補正だ」という結論の対比項となる。
extracting.context_sentence: Extracting the gas is mechanically simple, since crushing a fragment of ice in a vacuum releases it, and the resulting sample can be measured by the same instruments used on air collected yesterday.

mechanically.etymology: ギリシャ語 mēkhanē(装置) → mechanical + -ly
mechanically.definition: 機械的に、装置の面では。
mechanically.usage_in_passage: 分析化学的な難しさではなく物理的な操作の話であることを限定し、simple の意味範囲を絞る。
mechanically.context_sentence: Extracting the gas is mechanically simple, since crushing a fragment of ice in a vacuum releases it, and the resulting sample can be measured by the same instruments used on air collected yesterday.

crushing.etymology: 古フランス語 croissir(砕く) + -ing
crushing.usage_in_passage: "crushing a fragment of ice in a vacuum releases it" が気体回収の実際の手順を示す。
crushing.context_sentence: Extracting the gas is mechanically simple, since crushing a fragment of ice in a vacuum releases it, and the resulting sample can be measured by the same instruments used on air collected yesterday.

fragment.etymology: ラテン語 frangere(壊す) → fragmentum
fragment.usage_in_passage: 測定に要する試料が小片で足りることを示し、貴重なコアを損なわずに分析できることを含意する。
fragment.context_sentence: Extracting the gas is mechanically simple, since crushing a fragment of ice in a vacuum releases it, and the resulting sample can be measured by the same instruments used on air collected yesterday.

vacuum.etymology: ラテン語 vacuus(空の) → vacuum「空虚」
vacuum.usage_in_passage: 外気の混入を防ぐ条件として示され、測定の信頼性を担保する。
vacuum.context_sentence: Extracting the gas is mechanically simple, since crushing a fragment of ice in a vacuum releases it, and the resulting sample can be measured by the same instruments used on air collected yesterday.

collected.etymology: ラテン語 com-(共に) + legere(集める) → colligere + -ed
collected.usage_in_passage: "the same instruments used on air collected yesterday" が、古代と現代の空気が同一の手法で測れることを示し、証拠の直接性を裏づける。
collected.context_sentence: Extracting the gas is mechanically simple, since crushing a fragment of ice in a vacuum releases it, and the resulting sample can be measured by the same instruments used on air collected yesterday.

concentrations.etymology: ラテン語 com-(共に) + centrum(中心) → concentrate + -ion + -s
concentrations.usage_in_passage: 測定される量を特定し、二酸化炭素とメタンという具体的な気体名につなぐ。
concentrations.context_sentence: The concentrations of carbon dioxide and methane that emerge are not inferred from proxies.

carbon.usage_in_passage: "carbon dioxide" として、第4段落では温暖化との時間関係が論点になる主役の気体を構成する。
carbon.context_sentence: The concentrations of carbon dioxide and methane that emerge are not inferred from proxies.

dioxide.etymology: ギリシャ語 di-(二つの) + oxide(酸化物)
dioxide.usage_in_passage: carbon と結合して二酸化炭素を指し、本文で最も重要な測定対象となる。
dioxide.context_sentence: The concentrations of carbon dioxide and methane that emerge are not inferred from proxies.

methane.etymology: ギリシャ語 methy(酒) → methyl + -ane(飽和炭化水素を表す接尾辞)
methane.usage_in_passage: 二酸化炭素と並ぶ測定対象として挙げられ、測定の網羅性を示す。
methane.context_sentence: The concentrations of carbon dioxide and methane that emerge are not inferred from proxies.

emerge.etymology: ラテン語 e-(外に) + mergere(沈める) → 「浮かび上がる」
emerge.usage_in_passage: "The concentrations ... that emerge" が測定結果を指し、直後の否定文で性格づけられる。
emerge.context_sentence: The concentrations of carbon dioxide and methane that emerge are not inferred from proxies.

inferred.etymology: ラテン語 in-(中に) + ferre(運ぶ) → inferre「推論する」
inferred.usage_in_passage: "are not inferred from proxies" が本文の主張の核心で、Q2の設問対象。否定形で用いることで直接測定との差を際立たせる。
inferred.context_sentence: The concentrations of carbon dioxide and methane that emerge are not inferred from proxies.

proxies.etymology: ラテン語 procuratio(代理) → procuracy → proxy + -es
proxies.definition: 代理指標。直接測れない量を推定するための代用データ。
proxies.usage_in_passage: 気候学の専門用語として登場し、直後の tree ring や shell の例で具体化される。
proxies.context_sentence: The concentrations of carbon dioxide and methane that emerge are not inferred from proxies.

measurements.etymology: ラテン語 mensura(測ること) → measure + -ment + -s
measurements.usage_in_passage: 第2段落では "direct measurements" として証拠の強さを、第4段落では "not the measurements themselves" として補正との対比を担う。Q5の指示対象でもある。
measurements.context_sentence: They are direct measurements of ancient atmosphere.

ancient.etymology: ラテン語 ante(前に) → antianus → 古フランス語 ancien
ancient.usage_in_passage: "direct measurements of ancient atmosphere" が、時間的に遠いものを直接測るという本文の主張を一句に凝縮する。
ancient.context_sentence: They are direct measurements of ancient atmosphere.

distinguishes.etymology: ラテン語 dis-(分けて) + stinguere(刺す) → distinguere
distinguishes.usage_in_passage: "This distinguishes them from most of what is known about the deep past" が、氷床コアを他の古気候研究から切り分け、その特異性を明示する。
distinguishes.context_sentence: This distinguishes them from most of what is known about the deep past, which reaches us only through substitutes: the width of a tree ring standing for a summer, the chemistry of a shell standing for the temperature of the water that formed it.

substitutes.etymology: ラテン語 sub-(下に) + statuere(立てる) → 「代わりに置くもの」+ -s
substitutes.usage_in_passage: proxies の平易な言い換えとして機能し、続くコロン以下の二つの例を導く。
substitutes.context_sentence: This distinguishes them from most of what is known about the deep past, which reaches us only through substitutes: the width of a tree ring standing for a summer, the chemistry of a shell standing for the temperature of the water that formed it.

width.etymology: 古英語 wid(広い) → wide + -th。ゲルマン系
width.usage_in_passage: "the width of a tree ring standing for a summer" が代理指標の第一例で、量が別の量を代弁する構造を示す。
width.context_sentence: This distinguishes them from most of what is known about the deep past, which reaches us only through substitutes: the width of a tree ring standing for a summer, the chemistry of a shell standing for the temperature of the water that formed it.

chemistry.etymology: アラビア語 al-kīmiyā → alchemy → chemist + -ry
chemistry.usage_in_passage: "the chemistry of a shell standing for the temperature" が代理指標の第二例で、同位体分析による水温復元を指す。
chemistry.context_sentence: This distinguishes them from most of what is known about the deep past, which reaches us only through substitutes: the width of a tree ring standing for a summer, the chemistry of a shell standing for the temperature of the water that formed it.

shell.etymology: 古英語 sciell(殻)。ゲルマン系
shell.usage_in_passage: 海洋生物の殻を指し、古水温の代理指標として提示される。
shell.context_sentence: This distinguishes them from most of what is known about the deep past, which reaches us only through substitutes: the width of a tree ring standing for a summer, the chemistry of a shell standing for the temperature of the water that formed it.

ingenuity.etymology: ラテン語 ingenium(生まれつきの才) → ingenious + -ity
ingenuity.usage_in_passage: "Dating the layers demands more ingenuity" が第3段落の主題文で、測定の容易さと年代決定の難しさを対比する。
ingenuity.context_sentence: Dating the layers demands more ingenuity.

accumulation.etymology: ラテン語 ad-(に) + cumulus(積み重ね) + -ation
accumulation.usage_in_passage: 第3段落では年層の可視性の条件として、第4段落では気泡の閉鎖深度と誤差の大きさを左右する変数として現れる。
accumulation.context_sentence: Near the surface, annual accumulation is visible, and the layers can be counted much as one counts the rings of a tree.

visible.usage_in_passage: "annual accumulation is visible" が、浅部で年層を数えられる理由を示す。
visible.context_sentence: Near the surface, annual accumulation is visible, and the layers can be counted much as one counts the rings of a tree.

deeper.etymology: 古英語 dēop(深い) → deep + 比較級 -er。ゲルマン系
deeper.usage_in_passage: "Deeper down the layers thin under pressure" が段落内の転換点で、単純な計数が破綻する領域へ議論を移す。
deeper.context_sentence: Deeper down the layers thin under pressure until counting becomes impossible, and researchers must instead model how the ice has flowed, calibrating their calculations against markers of known age.

thin.etymology: 古英語 þynne(薄い)。ゲルマン系
thin.usage_in_passage: ここでは動詞として用いられ、圧力による層の薄化が計数を不可能にする過程を示す。
thin.context_sentence: Deeper down the layers thin under pressure until counting becomes impossible, and researchers must instead model how the ice has flowed, calibrating their calculations against markers of known age.

impossible.usage_in_passage: 計数という単純な方法の限界を明示し、モデル化という代替手段の必要を根拠づける。
impossible.context_sentence: Deeper down the layers thin under pressure until counting becomes impossible, and researchers must instead model how the ice has flowed, calibrating their calculations against markers of known age.

researchers.context_sentence: Deeper down the layers thin under pressure until counting becomes impossible, and researchers must instead model how the ice has flowed, calibrating their calculations against markers of known age.

calibrating.context_sentence: Deeper down the layers thin under pressure until counting becomes impossible, and researchers must instead model how the ice has flowed, calibrating their calculations against markers of known age.

markers.usage_in_passage: "markers of known age" が較正の基準を指し、直後で火山灰がその具体例として示される。
markers.context_sentence: Deeper down the layers thin under pressure until counting becomes impossible, and researchers must instead model how the ice has flowed, calibrating their calculations against markers of known age.

volcanic.context_sentence: Volcanic eruptions are especially useful, because each deposits a distinctive film of sulfate that appears simultaneously in cores from opposite ends of the earth and thus anchors separate records to a common chronology.

anchors.usage_in_passage: 語彙問題の対象語。錨の比喩で、浮動しうる年代モデルを既知の一点に留める働きを表す。
anchors.context_sentence: Volcanic eruptions are especially useful, because each deposits a distinctive film of sulfate that appears simultaneously in cores from opposite ends of the earth and thus anchors separate records to a common chronology.

chronology.context_sentence: Volcanic eruptions are especially useful, because each deposits a distinctive film of sulfate that appears simultaneously in cores from opposite ends of the earth and thus anchors separate records to a common chronology.

eruption.etymology: ラテン語 e-(外に) + rumpere(破る) → eruptio

eruption.context_sentence: A large eruption is in this sense a stopwatch pressed once and read in both hemispheres.

stopwatch.etymology: stop + watch。ゲルマン系の複合語
stopwatch.usage_in_passage: 噴火を「一度押されて両半球で読まれる計時器」に喩え、同時性という抽象的性質を身近な道具に置き換える。
stopwatch.context_sentence: A large eruption is in this sense a stopwatch pressed once and read in both hemispheres.

hemispheres.context_sentence: A large eruption is in this sense a stopwatch pressed once and read in both hemispheres.

complication.etymology: ラテン語 com-(共に) + plicare(折る) → 「折り重なってもつれること」+ -ation

complication.usage_in_passage: "One complication deserves emphasis" が第4段落の主題文で、それまでの明快な説明に留保を加える転換点となる。

deserves.etymology: ラテン語 de-(強意) + servire(仕える) → deservire「値する」
deserves.usage_in_passage: 著者が読者の注意を明示的に要求する語で、この段落の重要性を格上げする。

emphasis.etymology: ギリシャ語 en-(中に) + phainein(示す) → emphasis
emphasis.usage_in_passage: deserves と結びついて、続く内容が見落とされやすい要点であることを予告する。

roughly.etymology: 古英語 rūh(粗い) → rough + -ly。ゲルマン系
roughly.usage_in_passage: "roughly a hundred meters" が、閉鎖深度が場所により変動する概数であることを示し、後の誤差の可変性につながる。
roughly.context_sentence: Because bubbles do not close until the snow above has buried them under roughly a hundred meters of accumulation, the air in any layer is invariably younger than the ice enclosing it.

meters.etymology: ギリシャ語 metron(尺度) → ラテン語 metrum + -s
meters.usage_in_passage: 気泡が閉じるまでの深さを定量化し、時間差が生じる物理的理由を与える。
meters.context_sentence: Because bubbles do not close until the snow above has buried them under roughly a hundred meters of accumulation, the air in any layer is invariably younger than the ice enclosing it.

invariably.etymology: ラテン語 in-(否定) + variare(変える) → invariable + -ly
invariably.usage_in_passage: "the air in any layer is invariably younger than the ice enclosing it" が誤差の方向が常に一定であることを示し、補正が原理的に可能である根拠となる。
invariably.context_sentence: Because bubbles do not close until the snow above has buried them under roughly a hundred meters of accumulation, the air in any layer is invariably younger than the ice enclosing it.

younger.etymology: 古英語 geong(若い) → young + 比較級 -er。ゲルマン系
younger.usage_in_passage: 氷と空気の年代差という第4段落の核心を一語で表し、Q4の推論の出発点となる。
younger.context_sentence: Because bubbles do not close until the snow above has buried them under roughly a hundred meters of accumulation, the air in any layer is invariably younger than the ice enclosing it.

enclosing.etymology: ラテン語 in-(中に) + claudere(閉じる) → enclose + -ing
enclosing.usage_in_passage: "the ice enclosing it" が、比較される二つの対象(空気と氷)の物理的関係を明示する。
enclosing.context_sentence: Because bubbles do not close until the snow above has buried them under roughly a hundred meters of accumulation, the air in any layer is invariably younger than the ice enclosing it.

offset.etymology: off + set。ゲルマン系の複合語
offset.usage_in_passage: 空気と氷の年代差を名詞化した語で、以降 "The offset can exceed several thousand years" として定量的な議論の対象になる。
offset.context_sentence: The offset can exceed several thousand years where accumulation is slow, and it must be estimated and subtracted before gas and temperature can be compared.

exceed.etymology: ラテン語 ex-(超えて) + cedere(行く) → excedere
exceed.usage_in_passage: 誤差が数千年に達しうることを示し、無視できない大きさであることを印象づける。
exceed.context_sentence: The offset can exceed several thousand years where accumulation is slow, and it must be estimated and subtracted before gas and temperature can be compared.

subtracted.etymology: ラテン語 sub-(下から) + trahere(引く) → subtrahere
subtracted.usage_in_passage: "estimated and subtracted" が補正の具体的な操作を示し、単なる注意喚起ではなく手順であることを明確にする。
subtracted.context_sentence: The offset can exceed several thousand years where accumulation is slow, and it must be estimated and subtracted before gas and temperature can be compared.

distort.context_sentence: Failing to account for it would distort the very relationship the cores are drilled to investigate, since an apparent lag between warming and rising carbon dioxide might be an artifact of the sealing process rather than a fact about the climate.

investigate.context_sentence: Failing to account for it would distort the very relationship the cores are drilled to investigate, since an apparent lag between warming and rising carbon dioxide might be an artifact of the sealing process rather than a fact about the climate.

apparent.context_sentence: Failing to account for it would distort the very relationship the cores are drilled to investigate, since an apparent lag between warming and rising carbon dioxide might be an artifact of the sealing process rather than a fact about the climate.

warming.context_sentence: Failing to account for it would distort the very relationship the cores are drilled to investigate, since an apparent lag between warming and rising carbon dioxide might be an artifact of the sealing process rather than a fact about the climate.

comparatively.context_sentence: Much of the technical literature on ice cores concerns not the measurements themselves, which are comparatively straightforward, but the corrections that make them mean anything.
